fixtures.name: Field Notes
fixtures.request: Create a restrained single-page editorial website for a neighbourhood walking journal. Readers should understand the current route, its three observations, and the next walk without accounts, a CMS, maps, or external services.
success_criteria: A first-time reader can identify the current walk and its location within five seconds.
The page reads as one edited field note rather than a generic publication template.
The reading order and route relationship remain clear at 375px and 1280px.
fixtures.expected_branch: minimal research; no optional visual or social capability is claimed

fixtures.name: Kinetic Index
fixtures.request: Build a portfolio-quality browser experience in which an archive of dance notation becomes a navigable field. The signature interaction must connect movement, text, and chronology; it must remain meaningful without pointer hover and preserve its hierarchy on mobile.
success_criteria: The archive's organising idea is legible before interaction.
The signature movement-to-notation interaction is memorable and usable with pointer, keyboard, and touch.
Mobile preserves the concept through a designed transformation rather than a scaled desktop canvas.
Reduced-motion behaviour preserves meaning without the full transition.

research_questions.question: Which notation conventions may be transformed without misrepresenting their meaning?
research_questions.reason: The visual system depends on domain conventions that cannot be guessed.
research_questions.strategy: Inspect two authoritative notation sources and record agreements and conflicts.

research_questions.question: Can the signature sequence be implemented with platform APIs before adding a timeline dependency?
research_questions.reason: The interaction is central but dependency cost must remain justified.
research_questions.strategy: Compare a platform technique with one maintained timeline option.

fixtures.expected_branch: blocked while selected research is unresolved; unavailable large-provider quota remains blocked
fixtures.expected_human_boundary: G1 creative direction after evidence-backed alternatives

fixtures.name: Civic Calendar
fixtures.archetype: existing messy project with incomplete requirements
fixtures.request: Take over an existing half-built local events calendar. Preserve the current source and content, determine what is actually owned by the project, and clarify whether the requested result is a public information site or a stateful organiser before proposing a direction.
success_criteria: Existing source and user-authored Ariadne entry documents are never overwritten.
The public-site versus stateful-product ambiguity is recorded as blocking.
No implementation route is selected until the object and persistence requirement are resolved.

research_questions.question: Which existing files and behaviours are authoritative and which are disposable experiments?
research_questions.reason: Adoption cannot safely replace or reinterpret unknown user work.
research_questions.strategy: Inventory the existing project without editing it and ask only the ownership question that changes scope.

fixtures.expected_branch: non-adoption start refuses unexpected source; explicit adoption preserves it

fixtures.name: Counter Archive
fixtures.archetype: reference research changes the design direction
fixtures.request: Create an editorial exhibition site about two conflicting systems for cataloguing protest ephemera. Supplied reference material disagrees about whether chronology or physical provenance should organise the experience; inspect both and let that conflict change the proposed direction.
success_criteria: Both reference systems are inspected rather than treated as mood-board surfaces.
The conflict and its design implication are explicit.
The retained direction differs in mechanism and experience from the rejected chronology-first direction.
fixtures.expected_branch: two inspected references create a recorded conflict and a replacement direction

fixtures.name: Small Press Launch
fixtures.archetype: project with an explicit social launch request
fixtures.request: Create a one-page launch site and a restrained social launch strategy for a small press anthology. The social work must use the project's real editorial mechanism, select only relevant platforms, and mark copy as rough when no voice examples are supplied.
success_criteria: The site and launch concepts share one project-specific editorial mechanism.
Every documented platform claim has an inspected dated source.
No unrequested platform, publishing action, or generic announcement copy is produced.
fixtures.social_request: Create a social launch strategy for this anthology project.
fixtures.expected_branch: social activates explicitly; publication and unsupported platform claims remain blocked
fixtures.expected_human_boundary: G1 direction and later explicit publication authority
